speaker: Unknown
en: Canva's an amazing story.
zh: Canva 是一个精彩的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everyone here is familiar with us.
zh: 我想在座的每个人都熟悉我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to give us just like the quick update on where you guys are today?
zh: 你想给我们简单介绍一下你们如今的状况吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And in particular, I mean, we're going to spend a lot of time talking about AI, but what you guys are in the middle of at the moment.
zh: 特别是,我们接下来会花很多时间谈 AI,以及你们目前正在经历的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we were born, I guess, as a company in 2013, started the company with my wife, who's my boss.
zh: 好的,我们这家公司诞生于 2013 年,我和我妻子一起创办了这家公司,她是我的老板。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's always fun.
zh: 总是很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that's always the case, whether you realize it or not.
zh: 我是说,不管你意识到与否,情况总是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're in a similar situation, building a business with someone you've got a close relationship with.
zh: 你也处于类似的境地,和你关系亲密的人一起创业。

speaker: Unknown
en: But no, we've had an exciting 13-year run.
zh: 不过,我们这 13 年的历程很精彩。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in the middle of the biggest transition of our whole lives as a company in sort of taking Canva from a creative platform in the SaaS world to really being the combination of a creative platform, productivity platform, and intelligence platform in the AI world.
zh: 我们正处于公司有史以来最大的转型之中,把 Canva 从 SaaS 世界里的一个创意平台,转变为在 AI 世界里真正集创意平台、生产力平台和智能平台于一体的存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that comes with a lot of challenges and excitement, and it's, yeah, it's super fun.
zh: 这带来了很多挑战和兴奋,是的,非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did Canva get to scale?
zh: Canva 是如何做到规模化发展的?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the backstory of Canva?
zh: Canva 背后的故事是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: How you guys got massive?
zh: 你们是怎么做大的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all companies get massive by having the best product in the world that's ruthlessly focused on solving customer problems.
zh: 我认为所有公司能做大,都是因为拥有世界上最好的产品,并且毫不妥协地专注于解决客户的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then part of the special source was really our freemium model.
zh: 我们的特别之处之一,其实是我们的免费增值模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't try to over monetize too early.
zh: 我们没有试图过早地过度变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really, when we first launched Canva, there's a lot of people over there.
zh: 我们最初发布 Canva 的时候,那边有很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey everyone.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They snuck in.
zh: 他们偷偷溜进来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you could only buy images for a dollar, so it was very much a free platform with one dollar purchases, and then after a while we realized that we should add a subscription model to this, and that's when it really started to take off.
zh: 是的,当时你只能花一美元购买图片,所以它基本上是一个免费平台加一美元购买的模式,后来过了一段时间我们意识到应该加入订阅模式,那之后它才真正开始起飞。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we really always respected that free user base, and we really saw that as our word-of-mouth marketing channel, and it's that channel that's really always growing the business.
zh: 但我们一直很尊重免费用户群体,我们真正把它视为我们的口碑营销渠道,而正是这个渠道一直在推动业务增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you do a lot to engineer the virality, or did it come organically?
zh: 你们有刻意去设计病毒式传播,还是它是自然产生的?

speaker: Unknown
en: We did all the basic things, you know, I mean, obviously really building in seamless sharing.
zh: 我们做了所有基本的功课,你知道,很显然我们构建了无缝分享功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We never wanted to watermark the product and deprecate the experience of our free users in order to get that brand awareness more externally.
zh: 我们从来不想给产品加水印、去损害免费用户的体验,以此来获得更多外部品牌知名度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually thought the whole strategy was being very free, being very generous, giving people what they wanted.
zh: 所以我们实际上认为整个策略就是非常免费、非常慷慨,给人们他们想要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we saw a pattern over time and over the many years customers use Canva that
zh: 而且随着时间推移,在客户使用 Canva 的这么多年里,我们发现了一个规律,

speaker: Unknown
en: More and more of them would upgrade, particularly as we added more premium features.
zh: 越来越多的用户会升级付费,特别是在我们增加了更多高级功能之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more value they got, the more acceptance they had to pay.
zh: 他们获得的价值越多,他们对付费的接受度就越高。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about where you should...
zh: 你怎么看应该在什么时候……

speaker: Unknown
en: So most of your users are free users, and then the business bills are paid by the paid users, and so you're always drawing a graduation point, right?
zh: 你们大部分用户是免费用户,而业务账单是由付费用户支付的,所以你总是在画一条「毕业线」,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Where it's like, it's time to leave the nest, free user.
zh: 就是那种「是时候离开巢穴了,免费用户」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Flap your rings and become a paying Canva subscriber.
zh: 振翅高飞,成为 Canva 的付费订阅者。

speaker: Unknown
en: When are they ready to leave the nest?
zh: 他们什么时候准备好离开巢穴?

speaker: Unknown
en: We were very happy with our free-to-paid monetization rates forever, and they've always been very, very healthy.
zh: 长期以来,我们对免费转付费的变现率非常满意,它们一直都非常非常健康。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have a lot of education users that are essentially perpetually free.
zh: 我们还有大量教育用户,基本上是永久免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other than when they upgrade coming into college.
zh: 除了他们升入大学时升级付费。

speaker: Unknown
en: But AI has totally changed that because the cost of good to serve a user has gone from cents per month to now many, many more cents per month.
zh: 但 AI 彻底改变了这一点,因为服务一个用户的商品成本已经从每月几美分涨到了现在每月多很多很多美分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's really sort of changed the dynamics of the cost to serve and also sort of the dynamics of the business.
zh: 所以这真的改变了服务成本的动态,也改变了业务的动态。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, it's been an evolution.
zh: 不过是的,这是一个演变的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So concretely that means just for anyone, I mean we know this is Stripe, I'm sure a lot of you in the audience are feeling this, just building any kind of non-deterministic AI product that's a totally different kind of product than the free products they're replacing and so they come with a different monetization path and you can't just naturally import whatever the graduation path was from free to paid in the old product that has to be different in an AI-powered product.
zh: 具体来说,这对任何人来说都意味着——我们知道这是 Stripe,我相信在座很多观众都有切身体会——构建任何类型的非确定性 AI 产品,它是一种与它们所替代的免费产品完全不同的产品,因此它带来不同的变现路径,你不能直接照搬旧产品里那条从免费到付费的自然升级路径,这在 AI 驱动的产品里必须是不一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct, yeah.
zh: 正确,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the cost to create a design historically, it cost us essentially nothing.
zh: 历史上,创建一个设计的成本对我们来说基本上是零。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now if you're to use a full agentic loop and you're to do web research, you're to call a brand, you're to create a whole campaign being many different designs that
zh: 但现在如果你要使用完整的智能体循环,你要做网络调研,你要调用一个品牌,你要创建一整个包含许多不同设计的营销活动,

speaker: Unknown
en: Include images, graphs, all types of things, and then you have to deploy it, then you want to understand how that content is actually performing once it's been deployed.
zh: 包括图片、图表、各种类型的东西,然后你还必须部署它,之后你还想了解这些内容在部署之后实际表现如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: Intelligence needs to be run behind all of these things, and many different systems need to be connected, and all those tokens cost money, and so the cost to create a design before, which was essentially nothing, has now turned into sense, and that at hundreds of millions of users scale really has a fundamental sort of effect on the business that we've had to adapt to.
zh: 智能需要在所有这些事情背后运行,许多不同的系统需要被连接起来,所有那些 token 都要花钱,所以以前创建一个设计基本上为零的成本,现在已经变成了美分级别,而在数亿用户的规模上,这对我们的业务产生了根本性的影响,我们不得不去适应它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like in the discussion about AI, you know, we get asked about the effect of AI on payments, which, you know, we're happy to talk at length about, but I feel like as people talk about the effects of AI in the economy generally, design is often one of the examples that people use, you know what I mean, where it's like the robots eating the jobs example.
zh: 我感觉在关于 AI 的讨论中,你知道,我们会问到 AI 对支付的影响,这个我们很乐意详细聊,但我觉得当人们总体上谈论 AI 对经济的影响时,设计往往是人们使用的一个例子,你懂我的意思,就是那种「机器人吃掉工作」的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously it's much more complex than that because also you're empowering people to do their own design where they don't need a designer anymore.
zh: 显然事情比那复杂得多,因为你同时也在赋能人们自己做设计,他们不再需要设计师了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just have much more design happening.
zh: 你可以让更多的设计工作发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your grand unified theory for design in the age of AI?
zh: 你在 AI 时代的设计方面有什么大一统理论?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's very similar to when we launched Canva.
zh: 我认为这和我们推出 Canva 时非常相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before Canva, you only had the Adobe products.
zh: 在 Canva 之前,你只有 Adobe 的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were very difficult to use.
zh: 它们非常难用。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were only accessible by cost and by the actual need to learn these tools to less than 1% of the internet-using population.
zh: 无论从成本上还是从实际需要学习这些工具来看,它们只对互联网使用人口中不到 1% 的人是可及的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We introduced Canva, and there was a lot of sentiment, oh, Canva's destroying design jobs.
zh: 我们推出了 Canva,当时有很多情绪,说哦,Canva 在摧毁设计岗位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ultimately, we created hundreds of millions of more designers and lots and lots of opportunities.
zh: 但最终,我们创造了数亿名更多的设计师,以及大量的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we empowered those professional designers to build templates, submit them on our platform.
zh: 然后我们赋能那些专业设计师去制作模板,提交到我们的平台上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we are now one of the only platforms, if not the only platform, where you can generate with AI and reference templates created by real humans that we then pay those real humans for those input images rather than just training on the internet.
zh: 而我们现在是仅有的、即便不是唯一,也是为数极少的平台之一,你可以在其中用 AI 生成内容并引用由真人创作的模板,而我们随后会为那些输入图像付费给这些真人,而不是只在互联网上做训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we really believe human in the loop is critical, particularly when it comes to creativity, and we really believe in paying out creators for the beautiful content and the design trends that they're setting that people can leverage with AI.
zh: 所以我们坚信人在回路中是至关重要的,尤其是在创造力方面,我们也坚信要为创作者们付出的美丽内容和所引领的设计潮流付费,让人们可以用 AI 来利用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just maybe to go deeper on this, because I think, again, it's an interesting micro story for what's going on more broadly.
zh: 那么也许可以再深入谈谈这个,因为我认为,再说一次,这是一个有趣的微观故事,可以映照更宏观的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I agree that it's clearly the effect that Canva is making much more design possible.
zh: 我同意,很明显 Canva 带来的效果是让更多的设计成为可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for a given job, previously you needed to go get a designer to do it.
zh: 对于某项具体工作,以前你需要去找设计师来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, if you're a restaurant looking for a menu design or something, previously you needed to get a designer to do it.
zh: 你知道,如果你是一家餐厅,想做菜单设计之类的,以前你需要找设计师来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you do not.
zh: 现在不需要了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also the case that the number of design jobs has just gone up over time.
zh: 同时,设计岗位的数量也确实随着时间推移在上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for those designers, if you were previously designing restaurant menus, what are you doing now?
zh: 所以对于那些设计师来说,如果你以前是设计餐厅菜单的,你现在在做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: How has the design job changed?
zh: 设计工作是如何变化的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you now making Canva templates?
zh: 你现在是在制作 Canva 模板吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: For people whose full-time job is a designer, how has that work changed?
zh: 对于那些全职工作是设计师的人,这份工作是如何变化的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, especially in large organizations, designers are really becoming the brand architects and the design architects.
zh: 是的,尤其是在大型组织中,设计师正在真正成为品牌架构师和设计架构师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so similar to how designers in organizations, they used to create templates, now they can create mood boards, styles, brands for all their different sort of sub-assets within an organization.
zh: 就像组织中的设计师以前会创建模板一样,现在他们可以为组织内各种不同的子资产创建情绪板、风格、品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every campaign has its own sort of brand.
zh: 每个营销活动都有自己的一种品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they can empower the rest of the organization to either create with those templates or leverage those base bits of creativity, feed that into AI to create things for whatever they want, but within that same brand framework.
zh: 然后他们可以赋能组织的其他人,要么用那些模板进行创作,要么利用那些基础的创意元素,把它输入 AI 去创建他们想要的任何东西,但都在同一个品牌框架之内。

speaker: Unknown
en: Despite this obviously being true and the numbers are being what they are,
zh: 尽管这显然是事实,数据也摆在那里,

speaker: Unknown
en: You do still get this persistent robots are reaching all the jobs, design jobs under threat from AI.
zh: 你仍然会看到这种持续不断的说法:机器人正在触及所有工作,设计岗位受到 AI 的威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: The headlines still are what they are.
zh: 新闻标题依然如故。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that bother you?
zh: 这会让你困扰吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you go out trying to correct the record?
zh: 你会出去试图纠正这种说法吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you feel about the fact that people want to write a certain story?
zh: 对于人们想写某种特定故事这件事,你有什么感受?

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I presume in particular over Canva's history, a lot of people have been writing the story of Canva replacing designers.
zh: 再说一次,我推测尤其在 Canva 的历史上,很多人一直在写 Canva 取代设计师的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually hasn't been too heavy recently.
zh: 实际上最近这并不算太严重。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was more so when we launched.
zh: 在我们刚推出的时候更多一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, there certainly is that general sentiment, but just like with
zh: 但是的,确实存在那种普遍的情绪,不过就像

speaker: Unknown
en: When we launched Canva, we really think it does empower professional creatives to do more.
zh: 当我们推出 Canva 时,我们真心认为它确实能赋能专业创意人士去做更多的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, with AI, having on-brand content is actually more important than ever.
zh: 而实际上,有了 AI,拥有符合品牌调性的内容比以往任何时候都更加重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is so much AI slop out there that you really need custodians of the brand within organizations.
zh: 现在有太多 AI 垃圾内容,你真的需要在组织内有品牌的守护者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I still think the role of designers, brand designers, and anyone in that space really has a lot of value to add and are increasingly becoming more and more valuable.
zh: 所以我依然认为设计师、品牌设计师以及任何在这个领域的人,真的还有很多价值可以贡献,并且正变得越来越有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like a lot of AI tools have a certain aesthetic.
zh: 我感觉很多 AI 工具都有某种特定的美学风格。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you, people talk about with, you know,
zh: 比如你,人们会谈到,你知道,

speaker: Unknown
en: LLMs, they have this very distinctive writing style, right?
zh: LLM 们有一种非常独特的写作风格,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You've hit on a great point.
zh: 你说到了一个很棒的点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the quietly load-bearing part.
zh: 这里是悄悄承载关键的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so distinctive.
zh: 它是如此独特。

speaker: Unknown
en: And similarly, with visual styles, mid-journey, when the early image models had this particular aesthetic that it went for, I noticed that whenever AI builds a website, you've probably noticed there's like a default CSS that the AI-built websites really like going for.
zh: 同样,在视觉风格上,Midjourney——当早期的图像模型追求那种特定的美学时,我注意到每当 AI 搭建一个网站,你可能也注意到了,存在一种默认的 CSS,AI 搭建的网站特别喜欢往那个方向走。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think of as the visual style or kind of the design values that you're trying to inculcate in Canva's products?
zh: 你认为你在 Canva 产品中试图灌输的视觉风格或设计价值观是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well really what we really want to give optionality and these models can do amazing things but they can do even better things if you give them guidance.
zh: 嗯,真的,我们真正想要的是提供可选项,这些模型可以做出很棒的东西,但如果你给它们引导,它们可以做出更棒的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're a brand how do you set up the brand architecture to give the model that guidance so it adheres to what you want but also expresses creativity and the human can also express their creativity by adding more prompts and they can be visual prompts or written prompts and the combination of that brand architecture with the human interaction can lead to better outcomes that
zh: 所以如果你是一个品牌,你如何搭建品牌架构来给模型那种引导,让它遵循你想要的,同时也表达创造力,而人也可以通过添加更多提示词来表达他们的创造力,这些提示词可以是视觉提示词或文字提示词,而这种品牌架构与人的交互相结合,可以带来更好的结果,

speaker: Unknown
en: You can guide or you can let it be sort of massively creative.
zh: 你可以引导它,或者也可以让它进行大规模的创意发挥。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's about the inputs to what is generated that ultimately guides it to being the generic brand slot or things that are broader scale.
zh: 关键在于对生成内容的输入,它最终引导内容走向千篇一律的品牌套路,还是走向更广阔的格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: But can't it not always be in push?
zh: 但它不能总是在 push 模式下吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, if you're...
zh: 就是说,你知道,如果你在……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know buying a house and you're touring different houses at a certain point you maybe say oh this is the one I really like this but if you'd been asked to specify the house that you want you wouldn't necessarily have come up with all those you know design cues and so people maybe to some extent like picking and won't necessarily have they won't be able to prompt exactly what it is they want.
zh: 你知道,买房的时候你在看不同的房子,到了某个时刻你可能会说,哦,这才是我真正喜欢的,但如果一开始就让你描述你想要的房子,你不一定能想出那些设计要素。所以人们在某种程度上喜欢挑选,他们不一定能通过提示词准确说出自己想要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's exactly what we do.
zh: 这正是我们在做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've got over 165 million templates, images, and graphic assets on the library, and we really don't think the prompt box is the right vector for creating visual content.
zh: 我们库里有超过 1.65 亿个模板、图片和图形素材,而我们真的不认为提示词框是创建视觉内容的正确向量。

speaker: Unknown
en: People want to, oh, they don't know they want a psychedelic, retro, 80s-themed birthday party invitation, but when they see it, they're like, oh, jeez, I really like that, and they can use that as the input to then add their own content to and make it their own.
zh: 人们想要——哦,他们不知道自己想要一张迷幻复古 80 年代主题的生日派对邀请函,但当他们看到它时,他们会说,哦,天哪,我真的很喜欢这个,然后他们可以用它作为输入,再加上自己的内容,把它变成自己的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see.
zh: 我明白了。
